claim: Yahweh tells Abram to leave his country, relatives, and father's house for a land Yahweh will show him.
label: Abram is called to leave

claim: Yahweh promises to make Abram a great nation, bless him, make his name great, and says all families of the earth will be blessed in him.
label: Blessing and nations

claim: Abram goes as Yahweh had spoken, and the text states he was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
label: Abram departs at seventy-five

claim: Yahweh appears to Abram and says he will give this land to Abram's offspring.
label: Land to offspring

claim: After Lot separates, Yahweh tells Abram to look in all directions and promises the land he sees to him and his offspring.
label: Land viewed after Lot separates

claim: Yahweh says Abram's own offspring will be his heir, compares his offspring to the stars, and the narrator says Abram believed Yahweh and it was counted to him as righteousness.
label: Heir, stars, belief counted as righteousness

claim: Yahweh tells Abram that his offspring will be strangers and afflicted for four hundred years and that the fourth generation will return.
label: Four hundred years and fourth generation

claim: God says Abram's name will be Abraham because he has made him father of a multitude of nations.
label: Abram renamed Abraham

claim: God commands circumcision and calls it the sign of the covenant, with the eighth day specified for males.
label: Circumcision as covenant sign

claim: God renames Sarai as Sarah, promises a son by her named Isaac, and says he will establish his covenant with Isaac.
label: Sarah, Isaac, and covenant

claim: Sarah bears Abraham a son in his old age; Abraham names him Isaac and circumcises him at eight days; Abraham is one hundred at Isaac's birth.
label: Isaac is born and circumcised

claim: The narrator says God tests Abraham; Abraham is told to offer Isaac, is stopped, a ram is offered instead, and the divine messenger reiterates blessing and offspring language.
label: Abraham is tested; ram and renewed blessing

claim: Israel loves Joseph more than his other sons and gives him a special robe; his brothers hate him and cannot speak peaceably to him.
label: Israel's special love and brothers' hatred

claim: Joseph reports two dreams; his brothers hate/envy him, and his father rebukes him while keeping the saying in mind.
label: Joseph's dreams and family reactions

claim: Joseph's brothers conspire, strip him, put him in a pit, and the narrative reports Joseph being sold for twenty pieces of silver and taken toward Egypt.
label: Pit and sale for twenty silver pieces

claim: Joseph is bought by Potiphar; the narrator repeatedly says Yahweh is with Joseph and prospers his work, leading Potiphar to entrust the household to him.
label: Joseph in Potiphar's house

claim: Joseph refuses Potiphar's wife's repeated advances and says doing this would be a great wickedness and sin against God.
label: Joseph refuses Potiphar's wife

claim: Potiphar's wife accuses Joseph; he is put in prison; the narrator says Yahweh is with Joseph and gives him favor there.
label: Accusation, prison, and Yahweh with Joseph

claim: Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker dream; Joseph says interpretations belong to God, gives interpretations, and the outcomes occur; the cupbearer forgets Joseph.
label: Two prison dreams and outcomes

claim: Joseph tells Pharaoh that the answer is not in himself and that God will give an answer; he interprets the paired dreams as one message about seven years of abundance followed by seven years of famine.
label: Pharaoh's dreams and Joseph's interpretation
